profile.name: Hayley Matthews
profile.writeup:
Hayley Matthews is a dynamic all-rounder and the captain of the West Indies women’s cricket team. Born on March 19, 1998, in Barbados, she has become one of the most influential players in women’s cricket with her explosive batting, effective off-spin, and sharp leadership skills.


Matthews made her international debut at just 16 years old, playing her first Women’s One Day International against New Zealand in 2014. She quickly established herself as a key player for the West Indies, showcasing her aggressive stroke play and ability to contribute with the ball. Her breakthrough moment came in the 2016 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup final, where she played a match-winning innings of 66 off 45 balls against Australia, helping the West Indies secure their first-ever T20 World Cup title.


Over the years, Matthews has continued to be a cornerstone of the West Indies team. She has delivered standout performances across all formats, including career-best figures of 4/10 in T20Is and multiple match-winning innings in ODIs. Her ability to dominate with both bat and ball earned her leadership responsibilities, and she was named West Indies captain in 2022. Under her captaincy, the team has shown resilience and promise, with Matthews leading from the front in crucial matches.


Beyond international cricket, Matthews has been a sought-after player in franchise leagues around the world. She has represented teams in The Hundred, Women’s Big Bash League, and the Women’s T20 League, delivering consistent all-round performances. Her adaptability across different conditions makes her one of the most valuable players in women’s cricket today.


The year 2023 proved transformational for Matthews as she dominated across formats and leagues. In March 2023, she was selected to play for the Mumbai Indians in the inaugural Women’s Premier League. Bought for just INR 40 lakh, Matthews proved to be one of the shrewdest signings in WPL history. She scored 271 runs as MI’s third-highest run-getter and became the joint-highest wicket-taker in the entire tournament with 16 wickets, winning the coveted Purple Cap. Her all-round performances were instrumental in Mumbai Indians winning the inaugural WPL title, and she was awarded Player of the Tournament for her brilliance.


In October 2023, Matthews struck a scintillating 132 against Australia, her second T20I century and highest score in the format. During that series, she crossed the 2,000-run milestone in T20Is, cementing her status as one of the format’s leading batters. She won the ICC Women’s Player of the Month award for October 2023, recognizing her extraordinary performances.


The year 2024 saw Matthews embark on an extraordinary run in ODI cricket. She scored three ODI centuries during the year, including her career-best unbeaten 141. Her conversion rate of fifties into hundreds became remarkable, as she converted six consecutive ODI fifties into centuries, a record in women’s ODI history that surpassed the previous mark of four. With eight ODI centuries to her name by the end of 2024, Matthews had surpassed Sarah Taylor, Amy Satterthwaite, and Mithali Raj, who each have seven, and now sat level with Sophie Devine, Karen Rolton, and Laura Wolvaardt. 
 

Matthews was named as captain of the West Indies squad for the 2024 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup in the UAE. Though West Indies lost in the semi-final to New Zealand, Matthews’ leadership and performances throughout the tournament were commendable. In the WPL 2024 season, Matthews continued her excellent form for Mumbai Indians, playing crucial roles with both bat and ball as MI reached the playoffs. Her all-round contributions remained vital to the team’s success.


In April 2025, Matthews captained West Indies at the Women’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier in Pakistan, guiding her team through a crucial tournament as they sought qualification for the main event. She scored a century in one of the matches, playing key innings against teams like Pakistan and Thailand. 
 

In the WPL 2025 season, Matthews remained a core member of Mumbai Indians and played crucial roles in the team’s second title-winning campaign. Her ability to open the batting and bowl crucial overs with her off-spin made her one of the most valuable players in the competition. She continued to add to her tally as the most successful bowler in WPL history.


However, September 2025 brought a significant setback. During The Hundred in England, where she was playing for Welsh Fire, Matthews sustained a serious injury, tearing her shoulder socket. The injury meant Matthews was unable to participate in the Women’s Caribbean Premier League 2025, where she had been the leading run-scorer and wicket-taker for Barbados Royals in back-to-back title-winning campaigns in 2023 and 2024. 
 

Come the year 2026, Matthews continues to be a vital part of the Mumbai Indians setup, being retained by the franchise. Her experience at a young age continues to cater her side to success.
